name: Trins
kurzbeschreibung: A charming village in the Wipptal valley, featuring the idyllic Trinser Weiher lake and the Trinser Moor bog—a true gem for nature lovers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Trins is situated at an elevation of 1,233 meters in the lower Gschnitztal, a pristine western side valley of the Wipptal south of Innsbruck. Home to approximately 1,350 inhabitants, this charming mountain village occupies a sunny terrace and glacial moraine formations where the Trunbach and Gschnitzbach streams converge, enclosed by the Tux and Stubai Alps. Together with neighboring Gschnitz, Trins holds the distinguished title of 'Mountaineering Village' (Bergsteigerdorf) awarded by the Austrian Alpine Club—an accolade honoring sustainable alpine tourism without mechanical ski lifts, unspoiled landscapes, and authentic farming traditions. The village core features traditional clustered farmsteads, Rhaeto-Romanic historical traces, and facade frescoes adorned with exquisite Baroque Lüftlmalerei murals.

History

Settlement in the valley dates back to Bronze and Iron Age civilizations. Trins was first recorded in writing around 1030 AD as 'Trunnes' in the registry of the Prince-Bishopric of Brixen. From the High Middle Ages through the 17th century, mining for antimony, copper, and lead flourished here, drawing skilled miners who shaped the community's layout. On a moraine knoll on the valley floor stands Schloss Schneeberg castle: in 1500, Emperor Maximilian I enfeoffed his advisor Franz Schneeberger with the estate, which was acquired by the Counts of Sarnthein in 1778 and remains in their private possession today. Consecrated in 1494, the Parish Church of Saint George dominates a steep church hill. Its interior boasts ceiling frescoes painted in 1755 by Anton Kirchebner, portraying Saint George protecting a detailed historical panorama of Trins. Perched high above the valley floor on a sheer rock pinnacle at 1,661 meters, the pilgrimage chapel of Saint Magdalena houses the oldest Romanesque choir frescoes in North Tyrol.

Getting There

By car, travel via the Brenner Autobahn A13 to the Matrei/Steinach exit, or take the toll-free Brenner Federal Road B182 to Steinach am Brenner. From Steinach, state road L10 into the Gschnitztal reaches Trins in just four kilometers. Rail travelers use S-Bahn lines S3 and S4 from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof to Steinach am Brenner. From the railway station, regular VVT regional bus line 560 provides direct transfers to Trins.

Tips

Mount Blaser (2,241 meters) is renowned as a botanical sanctuary: thanks to its unique geology, it is celebrated as the most flower-rich mountain in Tyrol, blanketed in edelweiss, gentians, and alpine roses, with the cozy Blaserhütte refuge resting just below the summit. For alpine expeditions, the Padasterjochhaus refuge at 2,232 meters in the Stubai Alps commands panoramic vistas across the Wipptal. A short stroll from the village leads to the thundering Sarnthein Waterfall and the Adlerblick viewing deck. In winter, Trins delights Nordic skiers with cross-country trails tracing the tranquil valley floor.
